correctness.rationale: PASS. For scalar f(x)=lambda x^2/2, centered two-point Gaussian gradient estimate equals lambda*x*U^2, independently of smoothing, giving iteration product (1-a*Y_n) with Y_n~chi²_n/n. Strong law applies since gamma density has integrable log singularity; strict sign of F_n=E log|1-aY_n| determines almost-sure exponential contraction/divergence. Gamma integrations give F2=-e^{-1/a}Ei(1/a), F4=1-(1+2/a)e^{-2/a}Ei(2/a). At rational a=107/40 independent high-precision checks gave F2=-0.0035466158821146 and F4=+0.0064289610044474, consistent with actual verify.py rational Taylor bound method (Ei series, log expansion, alternating exp tail). Uniqueness of each n=2,4 root follows from signs and positive derivative when F4 zero. Gamma central moments E delta²=2/n, E delta³=8/n², E delta⁴=12/n²+48/n³ give F_n(2+c/n)=(c-4)/n+O(n^-2), with exponentially small gamma tails around the log singularity; local positive derivative yields a_n=2+4/n+O(n^-2). Separate mean-square factor yields exact b_n=2n/(n+2), gap 8/n+O(n^-2). No global n-root uniqueness asserted.
